description: Purine (A, G) and pyrimidine (C, T) base stacking in B-form dsDNA produces a strong π→π* absorption peak at 260 nm (ε ~6600 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹ per nucleotide). The 280 nm shoulder arises from aromatic amino acid-like contributions. Pure dsDNA has A260/A280 = 1.80 ± 0.05.
chromophore: Heterocyclic purine (A, G) and pyrimidine (C, T) bases
transition: π → π* aromatic base stacking transition
clinicalNote: Standard molecular biology quantification: A260 = 1.0 corresponds to ~50 μg/mL dsDNA. Pure dsDNA exhibits A260/A280 ≈ 1.80; protein contamination reduces this ratio. RNA gives A260/A280 ~2.0.

sources.citation: Sambrook J, Russell DW (2001) Molecular Cloning: A Laboratory Manual, 3rd ed. CSHL Press. Appendix B: Spectrophotometric determination of nucleic acid concentration.
sources.purpose: ε 6600 per nucleotide at 260 nm; A260/A280 = 1.80 for pure dsDNA
